'''Nancy L. Allbritton''' is a Professor of Bioengineering and  the Frank & Julie Jungers Dean of the College of Engineering at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="Holtz"/> She was previously a Kenan Professor and Chair in the Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] and [[North Carolina State University]].<ref name="Cellmicrosystems.com">{{cite web |url=https://cellmicrosystems.com/meet-the-team/ |title=Meet the Team &#124; Single-Cell Isolation and Recovery |publisher=Cellmicrosystems.com |date= |access-date=2017-05-01 |archive-date=2020-10-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021080447/https://cellmicrosystems.com/meet-the-team/ }}</ref>

She is best known for her work in single-cell analysis. Using engineering methods, Allbritton creates tools for better understanding and manipulating living cells and tissues. Microengineered platforms, microfluidics, and novel biochemical assays enable scientists to study [[cell signaling]] and [[signal transduction]] at the single-cell level.<ref name="UCDavis">{{cite web |date=October 30, 2014 |title=Distinguished Seminar Series: Nancy Allbritton, Professor and Chair Department of Biomedical Engineering University of North Carolina & North Carolina State University |url=https://bme.ucdavis.edu/events/distinguished-seminar-series-nancy-allbritton-professor-chair-department-biomedical-engineering-university-north-carolina-north-carolina-state-university/ |access-date=2 August 2018 |website=UCDavis Biomedical Engineering}}</ref>

==Education==
Allbritton received a [[Bachelor of Science|bachelor of science]] with a major in physics from [[Louisiana State University]] in 1979. She received a [[Doctor of Medicine|doctor of medicine]] from [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1985 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctor of philosophy]] in medical physics and medical engineering from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1987.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-04-27 |title=Nancy Allbritton {{!}} UW Bioengineering |url=https://bioe.uw.edu/portfolio-items/nancy-allbritton/ |access-date=2022-10-06 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Career ==
Allbritton was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at [[Stanford University]] from 1989 to 1994.<ref name="Washington" /> She then became a Professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]], teaching in the departments of Physiology and Biophysics, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Materials Science. She remained at UC Irvine for 13 years, from 1994-2007.<ref name="Washington">{{cite web |title=Nancy Allbritton |url=https://www.engr.washington.edu/facultyfinder/nancy-allbritton |website=College of Engineering |publisher=University of Washington |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

In 2007 Allbritton joined the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, becoming a Kenan Distinguished Professor.  From 2009-2019 she was the Chair of the Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and North Carolina State University.<ref name="Cellmicrosystems.com"/> 
She has held faculty appointments in Chemistry, Pharmacology and Applied Physical Sciences at UNC, and in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at NC State.<ref name="Lancaster">{{cite news |last1=Lancaster |first1=Brent |title=Allbritton leaving Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering |url=https://www.engr.ncsu.edu/news/2019/08/23/allbritton-leaving-joint-department-of-biomedical-engineering/ |access-date=8 September 2021 |work=College of Engineering News |publisher=NC State University |date=August 23, 2019}}</ref>

As of November 1, 2019, Allbritton became a Professor of Bioengineering and the Frank & Julie Jungers Dean of Engineering at the University of Washington College of Engineering.<ref name="AIChE">{{cite web |title=Nancy L. Allbritton |url=https://www.aiche.org/community/bio/nancy-l-allbritton |website=American Institute of Chemical Engineers |date=26 May 2020 |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref><ref name="Holtz">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Nancy Allbritton named dean of UW's College of Engineering  |first=Jackson |last= Holtz August 13, 2019|date=August 13, 2019 |url=https://www.washington.edu/news/2019/08/13/dr-nancy-allbritton-named-dean-of-uws-college-of-engineering/|access-date=2020-06-24|website=UW News|language=en}}</ref>

Allbritton was appointed a co-[[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry]]'' in 2021.<ref name="directory">{{cite web| url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?0000,anchem| website=Annual Reviews| title=Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry, Current Editorial Committee| access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref>

==Research interests==
Allbritton's interest in single-cell analysis have hinged on the use of [[capillary electrophoresis]] (CE) and microfabricated technologies. Through this work she has studied lipid signaling at the single-cell level, the isolation cytotoxic T-cells with specific properties, and the capture of colonic crypts. In the [[organ-on-a-chip]] field,<ref name="Ma">{{cite journal |last1=Ma |first1=Chao |last2=Peng |first2=Yansong |last3=Li |first3=Hongtong |last4=Chen |first4=Weiqiang |title=Organ-on-a-Chip: A New Paradigm for Drug Development |journal=Trends in Pharmacological Sciences |date=February 2021 |volume=42 |issue=2 |pages=119–133 |doi=10.1016/j.tips.2020.11.009|issn=0165-6147  |pmid=33341248 |pmc=7990030 }}</ref>  Allbritton has used fabrication technologies from [[electronics]] and [[microfluidics]] to develop devices that effectively recreate the environment of both the small and [[large intestine]].<ref name="Landhuis">{{cite journal |last1=Landhuis |first1=Esther |title=Microbial chemistry gains fresh focus |journal=Nature |date=26 September 2019 |volume=573 |issue=7775 |pages=615–616 |doi=10.1038/d41586-019-02853-5 |pmid=31551561 |bibcode=2019Natur.573..615L |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Organs">{{cite news |title=Researchers awarded $5.3 million to develop novel gut-on-a-chip technology |url=https://college.unc.edu/2015/10/gut-on-a-chip-technology/ |access-date=8 September 2021 |work=UNC College of Arts & Sciences |date=October 12, 2015}}</ref>  These include micro [[total analysis system]]s<ref name="Zhuang">{{cite journal |last1=Zhuang |first1=Jianjian |last2=Yin |first2=Juxin |last3=Lv |first3=Shaowu |last4=Wang |first4=Ben |last5=Mu |last3=Melvin |first3=Adam T. |last4=Dobes |first4=Nicholas C. |last5=Wang |first5=Yuli |last6=Dickinson |first6=Alexandra J. |last7=Gach |first7=Philip C. |last8=Shah |first8=Pavak K.
